leanRatingAvailability.summary: Indian outlets CANNOT currently be lean-rated the way Ground News rates US outlets, because the two systems Ground News attributes are not both usable here. AllSides — the more methodologically transparent of the pair (multi-partisan editorial reviews, blind bias surveys, three-person left/centre/right panels) — rates ~1,400 US outlets and states its ratings reflect the American political spectrum; its Indian coverage is negligible, and its pages returned HTTP 403 to our fetching, so no AllSides rating is recorded against any outlet in this file. Media Bias/Fact Check does publish attributed, dated, per-outlet left/right ratings for a substantial number of Indian titles (21 of the 27 outlets here), which is why the verdict is 'partial' rather than 'none'. But MBFC's own methodology page states that no universally accepted formula for measuring political bias exists, that its ratings are 'structured human assessments', and — decisively for this project — that its framework 'remains primarily tailored to the political landscape of the United States'. Its scoring is 70% weighted on economic system and social-liberalism-vs-conservatism axes drawn from US politics, one editor holds final authority, and it is not peer reviewed; a 2026 arXiv paper (Ruiz Iglesias et al.) argues researchers should stop using it. No India-produced, maintained, methodologically transparent lean-rating system was found. The three serious India-specific instruments measure something else: the Media Ownership Monitor India (RSF/DataLEADS) measures OWNERSHIP and last updated in 2019; the Reuters Institute Digital News Report India chapter measures TRUST and REACH among an English-speaking online sample; Lokniti-CSDS measures CONSUMPTION. One peer-reviewed-track paper (Agarwal et al. 2021) hand-labelled 103 Indian news sites Left/Right/Centre using two expert reviewers plus MOM data, but it is a one-off research artefact, not a maintained service. The practical consequence is that lean coverage is inverse to reach: the Hindi and regional-language mastheads and channels that dominate Indian audiences are the least rated. Recommended handling: render MBFC labels only with the rater's name, score, date and URL attached, never as a project-authored badge, and render 'no third-party rating exists' as loudly as a rating.

systems.name: Media Bias/Fact Check (MBFC)
systems.producer: Media Bias/Fact Check LLC (US); founded by Dave Van Zandt, one editor retains final editorial authority
systems.methodology: Human-driven scoring on a 0-10 bias scale mapped -10 (extreme left) to +10 (extreme right), weighted: economic system 35%, social progressive liberalism vs traditional social conservatism 35%, straight-news reporting balance 15%, editorial bias 15%. Separate factual-reporting score weighted: failed fact checks 40%, sourcing 25%, transparency 25%, one-sidedness/bias omission 10%. Updated methodology applied to all sources reviewed or re-reviewed from 1 Jan 2025.
systems.lastUpdated: 2026-08-04 (most recent Indian outlet re-review observed in this dataset: Alt News); individual Indian outlet pages carry dates from 2023-07-01 to 2026-08-04
systems.limitations: MBFC's methodology page states its framework 'remains primarily tailored to the political landscape of the United States', that 'no universally accepted scientific formula exists for measuring political bias', and that ratings are structured human assessments rather than objective measurement. Not peer reviewed; one editor holds final authority. A 2026 arXiv paper (Ruiz Iglesias, Witte Zimmerman, Fehr, Dodds, Danforth) argues MBFC 'represents the opinions of a single person', does not meet basic standards of academic rigour, and should not be used in research. Coverage of India skews hard to English-language titles and English-language websites of Indian-language groups: MBFC's 'ABP Live' entry rates abplive.com and its 'News18' entry rates news18.com, not the Hindi television channels; its 'Onmanorama' entry explicitly rates the English portal, not the Malayalam newspaper. Zee News, Dainik Jagran, Dainik Bhaskar, Malayala Manorama and Eenadu appear unrated. MBFC's India country profile is behind a paid membership wall.

systems.name: AllSides Media Bias Ratings
systems.methodology: Multi-partisan editorial reviews by trained reviewers, blind bias surveys in which participants rate content without seeing the source, small-group editorial reviews with a three-person left/centre/right panel, third-party analysis and community feedback. Rates online written political content; explicitly does not rate accuracy or credibility, and typically does not rate broadcast/TV or radio content.
systems.lastUpdated: unknown for Indian entries — AllSides pages returned HTTP 403 to automated fetching and could not be verified
systems.limitations: AllSides rates ~1,400 US news outlets and states its ratings reveal the average judgment of Americans across the US political spectrum. Indian coverage appears to be a handful of incidental entries at low or initial confidence, and search results suggest major Indian outlets are 'Not Rated'. Because allsides.com returns HTTP 403 to automated fetching, no AllSides rating has been entered against any outlet in this file — an unverified rating is worse than none. Its exclusion of broadcast content also disqualifies it for the Indian TV news market, which is where partisanship allegations concentrate.

systems.name: Media Ownership Monitor (MOM) India
systems.producer: Reporters Without Borders (RSF) with DataLEADS, funded by Germany's Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development (BMZ)
systems.methodology: Mapping exercise creating a public database of the owners of the highest-audience mass media outlets; at most 10 outlets per media type selected by audience reach; indicators harmonised with the EU-funded Media Pluralism Monitor of the Centre for Media Pluralism and Media Freedom (EUI Florence). Covers ownership structure, cross-media holdings, and risk indicators for concentration, transparency and political control.
systems.limitations: Does not rate political lean. Stale by seven years: it predates the Adani group's 2022-23 acquisition of NDTV entirely. Could not compute market-share concentration because Indian media companies frequently fail to file financial statements with the Ministry of Corporate Affairs. Could not compute TV audience concentration at all because BARC repeatedly declined to release annual viewership data, treating it as a corporate secret. Print audience figures rest on the Indian Readership Survey 2017.

systems.name: Reuters Institute Digital News Report — India chapter
systems.producer: Reuters Institute for the Study of Journalism, University of Oxford; India chapter authored by Anjana Krishnan (Asian College of Journalism, Chennai)
systems.methodology: Annual online survey of news users, reporting weekly reach and trust scores per news brand, platform usage and news-sharing behaviour.
systems.limitations: Measures trust and reach, not political lean. The India chapter explicitly states its findings are based on 'a survey of mainly English-speaking, online news users in India', representing 'a small subset of a larger, more diverse, media market', that results are not nationally representative, and that they under-represent the continued importance of traditional TV and print. The only lean-adjacent observation is directional and unquantified: brands 'either extremely critical or extremely uncritical of those in positions of power tend to have lower trust scores'.

systems.name: Lokniti-CSDS media studies ('Media in India: Access, Practices, Concerns and Effects')
systems.producer: Lokniti programme, Centre for the Study of Developing Societies (CSDS), with Konrad-Adenauer-Stiftung
systems.methodology: Nationwide face-to-face survey of media consumption behaviour: 7,463 citizens aged 15+ across 19 states and union territories, fieldwork January 2022. Sections cover household media presence, consumption patterns, social media engagement, news preferences, trust in news media, and media consumption vs political choices.
systems.limitations: Measures audience behaviour, trust and perception — not outlet-level political lean. Produces no per-outlet rating that could be attributed as a badge. Not fetched directly for this file (cited from search-result summaries of the Lokniti/KAS report pages), so treat the survey parameters as reported rather than documented.

systems.name: Agarwal et al. (2021), 'Under the Spotlight: Web Tracking in Indian Partisan News Websites'
systems.producer: Vibhor Agarwal, Yash Vekaria, Pushkal Agarwal, Sangeeta Mahapatra, Shounak Set, Sakthi Balan Muthiah, Nishanth Sastry, Nicolas Kourtellis
systems.methodology: Labelled 103 Indian online news websites Left, Right or Centre using two expert reviewers combined with data from RSF's Media Ownership Monitor, then measured third-party web trackers by partisanship.
systems.limitations: A one-off research artefact, not a maintained or updatable rating service, and five years stale. Labels rest on two expert reviewers — no inter-rater reliability statistic was surfaced in the abstract, and the per-outlet label list is not published in the abstract. Its stated purpose was studying web trackers, with partisanship as a covariate rather than the object of measurement. Not usable as an attributable public badge, and not used to populate leanRatings in this file.

outlets.ownershipNotes: Control passed from founders Prannoy and Radhika Roy to the Adani group across 2022-23 in four documented steps. (4) 30 December 2022: the 27.26% (about 1.75 crore shares) transferred to RRPR Holding at Rs 342.65 per share, roughly Rs 602.30 crore, through the NSE block-deal window; the Adani group's total holding reached 64.71%, with RRPR at 56.45% and VCPL at 8.27%. MBFC rates all three outlets on the right of centre (2.9, 3.2, 6.0) — the single largest same-owner cluster of same-direction ratings in this dataset, though with one rater and a US-calibrated scale that is a weak signal, not a finding.

crossMediaHoldings.owner: HT Media Ltd / Hindustan Times Ltd (KK Birla group, NSE: HTMEDIA)
crossMediaHoldings.note: HT Media operates print, radio broadcast and digital; 69.5% held by Hindustan Times Ltd. Also publishes the Hindi daily Hindustan (not separately catalogued here). Counter-example to owner-implies-lean: MBFC rates Hindustan Times Left-Center and Mint Least Biased under the same owner.

crossMediaHoldings.owner: Living Media India Ltd / T.V. Today Network Ltd (Purie family with IGH Holdings/Aditya Birla group, NSE: TVTODAY)
crossMediaHoldings.note: T.V. Today Network runs Aaj Tak, India Today Television, Good News Today and the group's digital properties (acquired from Living Media India Ltd); Living Media publishes India Today magazine. Ownership is split between a media family and a diversified industrial group's investment vehicle.

crossMediaHoldings.owner: Reliance Industries Ltd via Independent Media Trust (Network18, NSE: NETWORK18)
crossMediaHoldings.note: Network18 operates 25+ news channels across languages (News18 India, CNN-News18, CNBC-TV18), digital properties Moneycontrol and Firstpost, magazines including Forbes India, and History TV18 (JV with A&E Networks). Control by India's largest private conglomerate is exercised through a trust rather than direct shareholding.

crossMediaHoldings.owner: Adani Group via AMG Media Networks Ltd (NDTV, NSE: NDTV)
crossMediaHoldings.note: Acquired 2022-23 (see the NDTV ownership note for the four-step chronology). The second instance in this dataset of a diversified industrial conglomerate taking control of a national news broadcaster, after Reliance/Network18 in 2014.

Dainik Bhaskar (Hindi), Divya Bhaskar and Saurashtra Samachar (Gujarati), Divya Marathi (Marathi), plus radio broadcasting, internet/mobile services and event management.

Anandabazar Patrika and The Telegraph in print; ABP News, ABP Ananda, ABP Majha and ABP Asmita in television; magazines Sananda, Anandamela, Anandalok and Desh; digital properties ABP Live and regional editions. Also the original founder of Business Standard, sold to Kotak Mahindra in 1997.

crossMediaHoldings.owner: Zee Media Corporation Ltd / Essel Group (NSE: ZEEMEDIA)
crossMediaHoldings.note: 15 news channels (WION, Zee News, Zee Business and 11 regional) plus zeenews.com in nine languages. Promoter holding had fallen to 9.04% by June 2026, so 'Essel Group ownership' describes control-in-name more than equity.

crossMediaHoldings.owner: Malayala Manorama Company Ltd (Kandathil family, unlisted)
crossMediaHoldings.note: Malayala Manorama newspaper, Manorama News television and the English portal Onmanorama, plus magazines. Regional-language cross-media concentration of the kind MOM flagged: MOM recorded the top four Malayalam titles at 75.75% of that market's readership.

crossMediaHoldings.owner: Ushodaya Enterprises Pvt Ltd / Ramoji Group (unlisted)
crossMediaHoldings.note: Eenadu newspaper plus the ETV network of television channels. Founder Ramoji Rao died in June 2024; the post-succession control structure is not established here.

concentration.measure: Top-4 outlet share of newspaper readership, Hindi-language market
concentration.denominator: Hindi-language newspaper readership, Indian Readership Survey 2017; sampled outlets represent 73% of audience share
concentration.denominatorLabel: % of Hindi-market readership held by Dainik Jagran, Hindustan, Amar Ujala and Dainik Bhaskar
concentration.note: MOM India's headline print finding: four titles capture roughly three of every four Hindi newspaper readers. Base-rate caution: high top-4 shares are normal in language-segmented newspaper markets worldwide, so this figure is meaningful only against a cross-country control, which MOM does not supply.

concentration.measure: Top-4 outlet share of newspaper readership, by language market
concentration.denominator: Readership per language market, Indian Readership Survey 2017
concentration.denominatorLabel: % of each language market's readership held by its top 4 outlets
concentration.note: Punjabi 82.64%, Hindi 76.45%, Malayalam 75.75%, English 75.15%, Bengali 73.90%, Tamil 66.66%, Kannada 53.20%. The spread (53% to 83%) matters: concentration is a property of specific language markets, not of 'Indian media' as a single thing, and Kannada shows the same structure produces very different numbers.

concentration.measure: Cross-media ownership among the largest media companies
concentration.denominatorLabel: top 8 media companies analysed by MOM India
concentration.note: MOM scored cross-media ownership at 3 (highest risk band): 7 of the 8 largest owners are active in more than one media sector, with no regulatory thresholds limiting cross-media holdings. Base-rate reading: at 7/8 (87.5%), cross-media presence is NON-DISCRIMINATING among large Indian media owners — it characterises the sector rather than distinguishing any owner within it, so it should be rendered as context, not as an edge that implicates a particular group.

concentration.measure: Outlets, companies and individual owners mapped by MOM India
concentration.denominator: 58 outlets (25 print, 23 TV, 9 online, 1 radio) owned by 39 companies and 45 individual owners
concentration.denominatorLabel: highest-audience Indian media outlets, MOM sample, fieldwork Nov 2018 - May 2019
concentration.note: The only systematic public ownership map of Indian media, and it is seven years old — it predates the Adani acquisition of NDTV entirely.

DOCUMENTED VOID, rendered deliberately. MOM India could not compute TV audience concentration because BARC repeatedly declined to release annual viewership data, treating it as a corporate/industry secret; BARC publishes only weekly impressions for the top 5 news broadcasters in 10 language markets and reserves all rights over that data. The result is that India's most-alleged-to-be-partisan medium is also the one whose audience data is least available for independent analysis. MOM likewise recorded 'Missing Data' for radio, and 'No Data' for market-share concentration because Indian media companies frequently fail to file financial statements with the Ministry of Corporate Affairs.
srcs: MOM India — Aaj Tak profile (audience share: Missing Data)

concentration.measure: Size of the Indian media landscape (denominator for any 'concentration' claim)
concentration.denominator: 908 private satellite TV channels permitted and 1.55 lakh (155,000) registered publications, 2024-25; up from 821 channels and 1.05 lakh publications in 2014-15
concentration.denominatorLabel: MIB / Press Registrar General of India figures given in a Lok Sabha written reply, 24 July 2025
concentration.note: Essential counterweight: the outlets catalogued in this file are 27 of roughly 155,000 registered publications and 908 permitted TV channels. 'A few players control Indian media' is a claim about audience share, not about the number of licensed outlets, which has grown by about 48% in a decade. Any concentration finding must state which of the two it means.
srcs: Newsonair — MIB figures, Lok Sabha reply 24 Jul 2025

concentration.measure: Outlets in this dataset carrying any third-party lean rating
concentration.note: Our own count, not a third-party statistic. All 21 ratings come from a single rater (Media Bias/Fact Check); zero outlets carry a second, independent lean rating, so no inter-rater agreement can be computed for any Indian outlet. This is the central epistemic constraint on any lean UI in this project.

concentration.denominatorLabel: outlets in this dataset whose primary publication language is not English (Aaj Tak, ABP News, Zee News, Dainik Jagran, Dainik Bhaskar, Malayala Manorama, Eenadu)
concentration.note: Our own count. Only Aaj Tak is rated under its own Indian-language brand; the ABP rating evaluates the English site abplive.com. Zee News, Dainik Jagran, Dainik Bhaskar, Malayala Manorama and Eenadu — between them the largest-circulation Hindi, Malayalam and Telugu titles and a 15-channel news network — carry no third-party lean rating at all. Lean-rating coverage in India is therefore inversely related to audience size, and any lean visualisation built on it will systematically over-represent English-language digital media.

gaps: No India-produced, maintained, methodologically transparent outlet-level lean rating exists. Every lean label in this file comes from one US rater (MBFC) whose own methodology page says its framework 'remains primarily tailored to the political landscape of the United States'. Nothing here supports a project-authored lean badge.
Zero inter-rater agreement is computable: no Indian outlet in this dataset carries lean ratings from two independent systems.

AllSides — the more transparent of the two raters Ground News attributes — returns HTTP 403 to automated fetching (both allsides.com/news-source/* and the rating-methods page). Search summaries suggest Hindustan Times is rated Center at low/initial confidence and NDTV is 'Not Rated', but no AllSides value has been entered against any outlet because it could not be verified at source.

MBFC's India country profile is behind a paid membership wall, so the total count of Indian sources MBFC has rated could not be established; the count of 21 here is limited to outlets in this dataset.

MBFC ratings frequently target a group's English-language website rather than the named outlet: 'ABP Live' rates abplive.com not the Hindi channel, 'News18' rates news18.com not News18 India, 'India Today' rates the group's output not the TV channel, 'Onmanorama' explicitly excludes the Malayalam newspaper. Any UI must show the rating's actual subject.

The Media Ownership Monitor India, the only systematic ownership map, was last updated 28 May 2019 and predates the Adani-NDTV transaction, the Zee promoter-holding collapse and the Network18 promoter change. There is no successor.
BARC does not release annual TV viewership data for independent analysis, so TV audience concentration is not computable and MOM recorded it as Missing Data. Radio audience data is likewise missing.

Several Indian corporate and NGO domains blocked automated fetching, so primary-source verification was not possible and aggregator/tertiary sources were used instead: jplcorp.in (Jagran Prakashan), htmedia.in (HT Media), ndtv.com corporate pages, scroll.in/about, allsides.com, rsf.org — all returned HTTP 403 or were unfetchable. Listed-company shareholding in this file therefore comes from Screener.in (which aggregates exchange filings) rather than from NSE/BSE filings read directly; tiers were set accordingly.

article-14.com's About and Contact pages are JavaScript-rendered and returned only 'Loading...', so Article 14's publishing entity, legal form and funding are not established from any source. Recorded as ownerEntity: null.

Unlisted owners have no public shareholding pattern: BCCL (Sahu Jain family), Kasturi & Sons, Indian Express Ltd, Malayala Manorama Company, Ushodaya Enterprises, ABP Group, Delhi Press and ARG Outlier Media. Family control is credibly reported but percentages are unverified against MCA filings, which MOM notes are often not filed at all.
Ushodaya Enterprises shareholding (Ramoji Rao 42.26%, Cherukuri Kiron 28.36%, Cherukuri Vijayeswari 25.38%) is undated in the source and Ramoji Rao died in June 2024; the current split is unknown.

Business Standard's present-day shareholders are not disclosed — Wikipedia attributes ownership to Kotak Mahindra Bank via Business Standard Pvt Ltd, while MBFC records that the publication 'lacks transparency regarding current shareholders'.

Scroll.in's operating entity is inconsistent across sources (SCSN Pvt Ltd vs Scroll Media Inc, the latter incorporated in Delaware, USA); the India/US entity relationship is unresolved and relevant to foreign-funding questions.
Newslaundry's funding is described inconsistently: Wikipedia says subscription revenue only, MBFC names Omidyar Network. Unresolved.

Network18 promoter holding fell from 75% (March 2025) to 56.89% (June 2026) — a large change with no cause established here; it should be traced to the specific corporate action before being characterised.
Zee Media promoter holding of 9.04% (June 2026) is recorded but the history of the decline (pledges, invocations, dilution) is not traced.
Circulation and readership figures for Times of India, Malayala Manorama and Eenadu come from Wikipedia citing ABC/IRS rather than from the ABC certificates or IRS reports themselves.

Republic TV's MBFC ownership note is stale — it still lists Asianet News and Rajeev Chandrasekhar despite the May 2019 buyback. Rater ownership fields should not be used as ownership evidence anywhere in this project.
Lokniti-CSDS reports were not fetched directly; their survey parameters here rest on search-result summaries and should be re-verified before citation.

Coverage gap: this file omits Asian News International (ANI) and Press Trust of India (PTI), the wire agencies that supply much of the copy the rated outlets publish. Rating outlets while leaving their shared upstream unexamined is a structural blind spot.

rejected.candidate: The Balanced News, 'Political Bias in Indian Media: A 2025 Analysis of Major Outlets' (thebalanced.news)
rejected.reason: Self-published marketing content for the publisher's own news app. Names no external rater, cites no sources, academic studies or third-party ratings, and discloses no data, criteria weights or validation method behind its left/centre/right assignments. Assertions like 'NDTV has maintained its editorial character' are presented without verification. Exactly the sort of unsourced list the brief forbids copying.

rejected.candidate: AllSides ratings as a source of Indian outlet lean labels
rejected.reason: Methodologically the strongest candidate in principle — blind bias surveys and multi-partisan panels — but it rates ~1,400 US outlets against the American political spectrum, does not rate broadcast content (which is where Indian partisanship allegations concentrate), and its India coverage is a handful of incidental low-confidence entries. Its pages also return HTTP 403 to automated fetching, so nothing could be verified at source. Retained in `systems` for the record with coversIndianOutlets: false; contributes no rating to any outlet.

rejected.candidate: Agarwal et al. (2021) Left/Right/Centre labels for 103 Indian news websites
rejected.reason: Kept in `systems` for the record but NOT used to populate leanRatings. Two expert reviewers, no published inter-rater reliability, per-outlet label list not published in the abstract, five years stale, and partisanship was a covariate in a web-tracking study rather than the object of measurement. Not an attributable public rating.

rejected.candidate: Oxfam India / Newslaundry, 'Who Tells Our Stories Matters'
rejected.reason: A serious quantitative study (65,000+ articles and debates analysed; 90% of media leadership positions held by upper-caste Hindus; 3 of 5 bylines from General-caste authors) but it measures caste and gender representation in newsrooms, not political lean. Including it as a lean proxy would be a category error — newsroom composition is not editorial position.

rejected.candidate: Reuters Institute DNR trust scores used as a lean proxy
rejected.reason: The India chapter observes only that brands 'either extremely critical or extremely uncritical of those in positions of power tend to have lower trust scores'. That is a U-shaped relationship between trust and stance, not a directional lean measurement, and it is stated without per-outlet values. Converting trust into lean would be inference dressed as data.

rejected.candidate: Grokipedia, 'List of news media ownership in India'
rejected.reason: LLM-generated encyclopedia content with no editorial process or verifiable sourcing chain. Appeared in searches for ownership data; not used for any fact in this file.

rejected.candidate: Circulating 'godi media' lists and similar social-media outlet classifications
rejected.reason: Politically-motivated informal lists with no stated methodology, no named rater, no publication date and no revision history. They are a subject the project could legitimately document as a phenomenon, but they are not evidence of lean and must never be a data source.
Present on some Indian outlet articles, inconsistently sourced, edit-warred, and often citing opinion columns. Not a rating system and not attributable to any rater.

rejected.candidate: BARC viewership and IRS readership as lean evidence
rejected.reason: They measure reach only. Reach is retained in reachNote and concentration fields where sourced, and is never converted into a lean or partisanship claim.
